name: Burgundy

origin.place: New York State Agricultural Experiment Station, Geneva, New York, USA
origin.parentage: Sources differ: Macoun x Monroe (National Fruit Collection) or Monroe x (Macoun x Antonovka) (Orange Pippin)
origin.raised_by: New York State Agricultural Experiment Station

history: A very dark red early-autumn apple from the Geneva, New York breeding programme, introduced in 1974.

look.description: Large, round, glossy fruit almost covered in a deep, nearly black-red flush.

taste.summary: Crisp, sweet, subacid flesh that is often stained pink and browns quickly when cut. It does not keep: within weeks it softens and loses quality.

tree.notes: Vigorous, regular-bearing spur type; fruit hangs on the tree for about three weeks after ripening.

pollination.notes: Brogdale dates put it in group 4; Orange Pippin lists group 3. A good pollinator for others.

climate.best_climates: Cold-winter, cool-to-warm summer regions like upstate New York.

health.other: Poor disease resistance overall: scab, powdery mildew and cedar-apple rust, and very susceptible to fire blight.

grow_notes: Best for home growers who can spray and who will eat the fruit fresh within a few weeks. Avoid areas with heavy fire-blight pressure.

name: Bushey Grove

origin.raised_by: Good family of Bushey Grove (NFC names Mrs Good; Orange Pippin J.T. Good)

history: Raised in 1897 at Bushey Grove in Hertfordshire and introduced around 1926 by G.W. King of Sidcup, Kent. It received an RHS Award of Merit in 1922.

look.description: Medium to large, broadly conical fruit, greenish yellow with red stripes.

taste.summary: Very soft, coarse, very juicy flesh with a sharp acidity; a cooker that cooks well.

tree.notes: Vigorous, heavy-cropping tree with attractive blossom; spreading to drooping habit.

climate.best_climates: South-east English conditions like its Hertfordshire home, ideally on a dry, airy site.
climate.poor_climates: Wet, humid areas where scab is severe.

grow_notes: A heavy-cropping early cooker; give it an open, airy position and clear fallen leaves to keep scab down.

name: Carlton

origin.place: New York State Agricultural Experiment Station, Geneva, New York, USA
origin.parentage: Autumn Bough x Red Astrachan per the National Fruit Collection (Montgomery x Red Astrachan is also reported)
origin.raised_by: Richard Wellington, New York State Agricultural Experiment Station

history: Raised in 1912 by Richard Wellington at Geneva, New York, and introduced in 1923 as a late-summer red apple. It is a parent of Niagara and Redhook.

look.description: Medium to large, conical, ribbed fruit, dull yellowish green flushed brownish red and streaked brighter red, with russet dots.

taste.summary: Firm, fine flesh with a subacid flavour leaning slightly acid; low in aroma. A summer apple for eating soon after picking.

tree.notes: Spreading habit at Brogdale; little other data.

climate.best_climates: Cold-winter north-eastern US conditions like upstate New York.

grow_notes: A late-summer eating apple for collections; plant with an early-flowering partner and use the fruit promptly.

name: Carola
history: Bred at the Müncheberg fruit research station in East Germany and released in 1962; the National Fruit Collection holds it under the name Kalco.

look.description: Medium to large, flat-conical fruit with prominent ribs at the eye, lemon yellow with red flushing and stripes on the sunny side.

taste.summary: Very juicy, medium-firm, yellowish flesh with a lively sweet, subacid flavour and a fine Cox-like aroma. Eat it from the tree or within a couple of months.

tree.notes: Medium vigour at first, weaker with age. Crops very early, sometimes in the second year, and heavily, but tends to alternate after big crops; thinning helps.

pollination.notes: Mid-season (group 3). German sources list Alkmene, Cox, James Grieve, Goldparmäne, Idared and Oldenburg as suitable partners.

climate.best_climates: Central European continental climates on open, fertile soils.

health.other: Prone to bitter pit, water core and storage rots; moderately susceptible to scab and mildew; fruit bruises easily.

grow_notes: A precocious, productive Cox-type for garden trees; thin heavy crops to limit biennial bearing and handle fruit gently. Give it open, fertile soil.
